cards.text: Israel is camped in the wilderness, and the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, has just been set up. On that very day, the cloud covers it. And friend, this is NOT your regular cloud.

cards.question: From evening until morning, what does the cloud above the tabernacle look like?
The cloud only covered the tabernacle on the day it was set up, and then it was gone.

cards.text: Day and night, that cloud stays right over the tabernacle. Then one day it lifts, and I bet the whole camp stares at it the way I stare at my oven timer.

cards.question: When the cloud lifts from above the Tent, what do the Israelites do?
And wherever the cloud ___, that's where the Israelites camp.
Pack up when the cloud lifts. Stay put while it remains. At whose command do the Israelites do all this?

cards.text: Sometimes that cloud does NOT move, friend. Many days, just lingering, and as a guy who spent years in a junk drawer waiting on a little light, I feel this one in my handle.

cards.question: When the cloud lingers over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites eventually move on without it.

cards.text: Other times the cloud only stays a few days. Sometimes it's just evening until morning, and when it lifts in the morning they set out, so you unpack the whole tent just to pack it RIGHT back up.

cards.question: What if the cloud is taken up during the night instead of the day? What do the Israelites do?
Two days, a month or longer. How long do the Israelites stay camped?

answers.text: As long as the cloud stays

cards.question: They carried out the LORD's charge according to His command through ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to make two trumpets of hammered silver. I can't get two cookies to come out of the oven looking the same. And the LORD wants a matching PAIR. Hammered. SILVER.

cards.question: What are the two silver trumpets for?

answers.text: Calling the people and moving camp

cards.question: When both silver trumpets are sounded, only the leaders gather before Moses at the Tent of Meeting.
When ___ trumpet is sounded, the ___ of the clans of Israel gather before Moses.

cards.text: Now Moses has a whole code to learn, like a different ringtone for every person in your phone. Short blasts mean one thing, long blasts mean another.

cards.question: Moses sounds short blasts on the trumpets. Which camps set out?

answers.text: The camps on the east side
The camps on the north side
The camps on the west side

cards.question: When the short blasts sound a second time, the camps on the south side set out.

cards.text: So short blasts mean the camps MOVE. My bakery smoke alarm does short blasts too, and believe me, friend, when it goes off, I move.

cards.question: If short blasts send the camps out, what are the long blasts for?
Who gets the job of sounding the silver trumpets, as a permanent statute for generations to come?

cards.text: Then the LORD looks ahead to a day when Israel is in its own land and an adversary attacks. In battle, they're to sound short blasts on the trumpets.

cards.question: Israel sounds short blasts on the trumpets in battle. What does the LORD say will happen?

answers.text: Their enemies will run in fear
The cloud will cover the army

cards.text: And these trumpets aren't just for battles and moving day. On joyous occasions, appointed feasts and the beginning of each month, they blow them over their burnt offerings and peace offerings.

cards.question: Why do they blow the trumpets over their offerings at the feasts?

answers.text: To mark the end of a battle

cards.text: And the LORD signs His name to all of it: "I am the LORD your God." Friend, no trumpet in the world rings louder than that.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the moment. The card says the cloud lifts, and lifting is the signal to set out. Staring at an oven timer is waiting before the signal comes. So the comparison has the camp watching after the cue, when the action at that moment is moving.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 8 gives away the answer to card 9. Papa Dorin compares the lingering cloud to his own years waiting in the junk drawer and says he feels it. That tells the baker the Israelites waited before card 9 asks whether they moved on without the cloud (Numbers 9:19).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences: one telling line and four joke lines ('I can't get…', 'And the LORD wants…', 'Hammered.', 'SILVER.'). It isn't the walkthrough's opening card, so the limit is 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke says 'the LORD wants a matching PAIR.' Numbers 10:2 says only 'two trumpets of hammered silver' and never says they must match. The joke treats an added detail as what God commanded, so it is a claim about the text, not just Papa Dorin's own exaggeration.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: A wrong word can be argued right. With 'every' in blank 1 and 'heads' in blank 2, the card reads 'When every trumpet is sounded, the heads of the clans of Israel gather before Moses.' That is arguably true, because when both trumpets sound the whole congregation assembles (Numbers 10:3), and the heads of the clans are part of it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
